QUOTE: Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)` expands to `private_foo`. The struct declares the field as `private_foo`, so application code that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile with "no member named foo".
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming the member to `private_foo`, so `ctx->foo` fails to compile. The struct layout is not hidden. It is a rename, and anyone can define the macro to get the real name back.
